text: LiteRT-LM at agello-next 7b872544 pins Bazel 7.6.1 in .bazelversion (Google's build guide asks for the same version), and its .bazelrc disables bzlmod with `common --noenable_bzlmod`, so the build runs in WORKSPACE mode.
LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc applies `build --spawn_strategy=standalone` and `build -c opt` to every build by default.

LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc sets `build --enable_platform_specific_config`; Bazel then enables the `build:<host OS>` lines for the host, so on a Mac host the `build:macos` block (including `--linkopt=-Wl,-undefined,dynamic_lookup`) applies.

sources.quote: if the host OS is Linux and the `build` command is run, the `build:linux` configuration will be automatically enabled.

text: LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc ends with try-import lines for .tf_configure.bazelrc, xla_configure.bazelrc, %workspace%/.bazelrc.user and warnings.bazelrc, which Bazel skips when the files are absent.

agello/build-xcframework.sh (agello-next) exports AGELLO_BUILD_FLAGS="--config=agello -c opt <extra args>", runs `bazelisk build --config=agello -c opt "$@" //agello:CLiteRTLM`, deletes dist/CLiteRTLM.xcframework and unzips bazel-bin/agello/CLiteRTLM.xcframework.zip into dist/.

The `build:agello` block in LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc (agello-next, ours) defines LITERT_LM_FST_CONSTRAINTS_DISABLED=1, sets C++20 for C++ and gnu++20 for Objective-C++, links with -Wl,-undefined,error, and sets --workspace_status_command=agello/workspace_status.sh; the define matches //build_config:fst_constraints_disabled_by_define, which makes //build_config:disable_fst_constraints true.

`build:agello` sets `--cxxopt=-std=c++20 --host_cxxopt=-std=c++20` and `--objccopt=-std=gnu++20`; its comment gives the reason as Abseil's status API differing between C++17 and C++20, with build:macos setting C++20 for C++ only.
`build:agello` adds `--linkopt=-Wl,-undefined,error`, while LiteRT-LM's build:macos config links with `-Wl,-undefined,dynamic_lookup` (for target and host).
`build:agello` sets `--workspace_status_command=agello/workspace_status.sh`, the script that produces the STABLE_AGELLO_* keys behind litert_lm_get_build_info.

agello/build-xcframework.sh writes dist/BUILD-INFO.txt with the LiteRT-LM commit (plus ' (modified)' for a dirty tree), the LiteRT and ML Drift sources (a .bazelrc.user override's checkout or the WORKSPACE pin), the Bazel and Xcode versions, the flags, the build id from bazel-out/stable-status.txt, the UTC date, and the SHA-256 of each slice's CLiteRTLM binary.
//build_config:disable_npu_backend is true when the NPU flag or define disables it, on @platforms//os:ios, or when LiteRT's build_include is cpu_only; macOS is not in the group.

At upstream base df6df5b8, LiteRT-LM's //runtime/executor:default_static_gpu_accelerator has no dependencies in either branch of its select (dynamic link mode or default), so open-source builds link no GPU accelerator statically.

In agello-next (ours, 43f0f5c3), default_static_gpu_accelerator depends on apple_static_gpu_accelerator unless @litert//litert:litert_runtime_link_mode_dynamic; apple_static_gpu_accelerator, only for @platforms//os:ios and @platforms//os:macos, depends on @litert//litert/runtime/accelerators/gpu:ml_drift_metal_accelerator and links -framework Metal and -framework Foundation, and is empty elsewhere.
//runtime/core:engine_advanced_impl depends on //runtime/components:default_static_gpu_samplers and //runtime/executor:default_static_gpu_accelerator.

At agello-next 7b872544, //runtime/components:default_static_gpu_samplers is empty in both branches of its select, so the documented build links no GPU sampler, while Google's v0.18.0 iOS binary contains the closed TopK Metal sampler (39 defined symbols against 7 in ours, per generated/binaries.md).

text: LiteRT's litert_accelerator_library macro defines a static cc_library with alwayslink and defines = [LITERT_USE_STATIC_LINKED_GPU_ACCELERATOR]; //litert/runtime/accelerators/gpu:ml_drift_metal_accelerator is declared with this macro.

Under LITERT_USE_STATIC_LINKED_GPU_ACCELERATOR, LiteRT's ml_drift_metal_accelerator.cc runs a static initializer (StaticGpuAcceleratorInitializer) that sets LiteRtStaticLinkedAcceleratorGpuDef = &LiteRtAcceleratorImpl.

LiteRT's RegisterGpuAccelerator first registers an accelerator passed in the environment option kLiteRtEnvOptionTagSystemGpuAcceleratorHandle, then, if none was registered, LiteRtStaticLinkedAcceleratorGpuDef (logging 'Statically linked GPU accelerator registered.'), and only then tries to dlopen the names in kGpuAcceleratorLibs.

LiteRT-LM agello-next's WORKSPACE (ours) declares @litert as an http_archive of https://github.com/PowerBeef/LiteRT/archive/<AGELLO_LITERT_COMMIT>.tar.gz with AGELLO_LITERT_COMMIT = 362759838e34e1525f1cc27daddaf663a193c059 and sha256 dd8d2dc491cbd7c294113747e2a068ff416c4a2bd181bfaa5c4f5c92d971c312.

Upstream base df6df5b8 declares @litert as Google's archive at LITERT_REF with patch_cmds that rewrite @//third_party/ labels; at agello-next 7b872544 LITERT_REF and LITERT_SHA256 remain at the top of WORKSPACE but the @litert http_archive uses AGELLO_LITERT_COMMIT and AGELLO_LITERT_SHA256 instead.
agello-next declares @agello_telemetry as a local_repository at agello/telemetry, and //c:engine depends on @agello_telemetry//:telemetry and //agello:build_info.

agello-next's WORKSPACE declares XNNPACK at d89ef6669a14db203b3b7935b1b3862cb63fb6df with patch //agello/patches:xnnpack_qs8_qc8_scales.patch, before tf_workspace2() so TensorFlow's own XNNPACK declaration is skipped; the comment describes the patch as upstream XNNPACK c72e2a4ae0 (per-channel scales sized for the batch matmul).
agello-next's WORKSPACE declares FP16 (commit 4dfe081c...) with a build file that adds an alias target named fp16, before TensorFlow's workspace macros.

LiteRT-LM's WORKSPACE pins org_tensorflow at a1179d3c224967bd979950b823d5ce2a7e8f4c94 with third_party/tensorflow/tensorflow.patch, and com_google_absl at 20260526.0 with third_party/abseil/abseil.patch.
LiteRT-LM's WORKSPACE uses rules_apple 3.22.0, rules_swift 2.9.0, apple_support 1.23.1 and rules_rust 0.61.0; Cargo.toml pins llguidance =1.3.0, minijinja =2.14.0 and tokenizers =0.21.0.

agello/workspace_status.sh and agello/build-xcframework.sh read override lines of the form `build "--override_repository=<name>=<dir>"` from .bazelrc.user with sed (the last match wins) and report that checkout's commit; without one they report AGELLO_LITERT_COMMIT or ML_DRIFT_COMMIT from WORKSPACE.
LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc try-imports %workspace%/.bazelrc.user; the file isn't tracked in the repository.

In the documented re-pin order (build with .bazelrc.user overrides, then edit the tracked WORKSPACE pins, then rebuild without overrides), the rebuilt CLiteRTLM is not byte-identical: agello/workspace_status.sh stamps the LiteRT-LM commit with '+<hash of git diff HEAD>' for uncommitted changes and derives the build id from it, and make_build_info.sh writes both into kAgelloBuildInfoJson, which litert_lm_get_build_info returns and //c:engine links; so the litert_lm field and build id change between the two builds.

agello/release-xcframework.sh exits with code 2 if .bazelrc.user has an active `build "--override_repository` line or if `git diff --quiet HEAD` reports uncommitted changes.

agello/release-xcframework.sh builds with build-xcframework.sh and writes dist/release/<tag>/ with CLiteRTLM.xcframework.zip, checksum.txt from `swift package compute-checksum`, a Package.swift whose `path: "dist/CLiteRTLM.xcframework"` line is replaced by the release URL and checksum (failing if not replaced), BUILD-INFO.txt, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and NOTES.md.

Without --publish, agello/release-xcframework.sh stops after writing the files (a dry run); with --publish it runs `gh release create <tag> --repo PowerBeef/agello-litert-lm --target <commit>` uploading the zip, checksum, notices and build info; its header says publishing needs the user's OK.
As of 2026-10-15 the repository PowerBeef/agello-litert-lm has no GitHub releases.

Agello's Vendor/use-release-litert.sh (at 93122b6) requires REF and TAG, downloads checksum.txt from the PowerBeef/agello-litert-lm release TAG, vendors REF with refresh-litert-lm.sh, and rewrites the binary target's `path: "dist/CLiteRTLM.xcframework"` to the release URL and checksum.

Agello's Vendor/use-local-litert.sh (at 93122b6) copies Package.swift, LICENSE and swift/ from a LiteRT-LM checkout (default ../agello-arms/next/LiteRT-LM) plus its dist/CLiteRTLM.xcframework and BUILD-INFO.txt into Vendor/LiteRT-LM/dist, and deletes stale CLiteRTLM-*.pcm modules and CLiteRTLM.framework products in DerivedData.

text: LiteRT-LM's //build_config:disable_npu_backend matches @platforms//os:ios, and when it is true the //runtime/executor:llm_litert_compiled_model_executor_factory gets the define LITERT_DISABLE_NPU and doesn't depend on llm_litert_npu_compiled_model_executor; macOS is not in the group.

The Kotlin API's sealed class Backend has CPU(threadCount), GPU, NPU(nativeLibraryDir) and GOOGLE_TENSOR (name GOOGLE_TENSOR_ARTISAN); nativeLibraryDir is the directory holding the NPU libraries (e.g. the Android app's nativeLibraryDir).

The Kotlin JNI library litertlm_jni (a linkshared cc_binary) includes c/engine.h and also C++ runtime headers such as runtime/engine/engine.h, runtime/conversation/conversation.h and runtime/engine/engine_settings.h.
LiteRT-LM's Google Tensor backend config_settings (by flag or GOOGLE_TENSOR_ENABLED define) both require @platforms//os:android.
The Python package litert_lm loads liblitert-lm.so/.dylib or litert-lm.dll with ctypes.CDLL and calls the LiteRT-LM C API.

LiteRT-LM's Python package copies libGemmaModelConstraintProvider, libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator, libLiteRtTopKWebGpuSampler and libLiteRt from prebuilt/linux_* or prebuilt/macos_arm64 into the wheel, so Python on macOS uses the WebGPU accelerator rather than Metal.
The web SDK @litert-lm/core has its own version (0.12.1 at the pin) and its download script fetches the WebAssembly files from https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@litert-lm/core@<version>/wasm.

LiteRT-Omni (omni/) is LiteRT-LM's multimodal streaming runtime for ASR, TTS and text-to-image, with OmniEngine, OmniSession and MultiStagedSession pipelines; its README describes model parameters carried in .litertlm metadata (AsrMetadata, TtsMetadata, Text2ImageMetadata).

LiteRT-LM's .bazelrc defines LITERT_DISABLE_OPENCL_SUPPORT for build:linux and build:windows, builds Windows monolithic, enables YNNPACK for linux_arm64, and builds Android fully static with OpenCL support re-enabled.
On Android, LiteRT's RegisterGpuAccelerator tries libLiteRtGpuAccelerator, then (with OpenCL support) the CL/GL and OpenCL accelerators, then (with WebGPU support) libLiteRtWebGpuAccelerator.
